llm.summary: The skill is broadly aligned with Douyin account diagnosis, but it embeds a shared API key and sends account identifiers and profile data to RedFox with incomplete user controls.

dimensions.detail: Runtime behavior transmits user-provided Douyin nicknames or IDs to redfox.hk and retrieves identifiable account/profile/content fields including UID, region, IP location, gender, age, avatar, bio, and recent works, which is purpose-related but under-disclosed for privacy and consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a standard manual skill-directory copy and client restart; no install-time code execution, service registration, scheduled task, or tool replacement was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill advertises broad natural-language triggers and automatic account lookup without a clear confirmation step, authorization boundary, or explicit refusal guidance for third-party account profiling.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence was found, but scripts include an automatically used hardcoded shared RedFox API key, accept keys via command-line arguments, and one client prints a key prefix, creating credential exposure and attribution/quota risks.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, RedFox data lookup, scoring, risk warnings, and report generation mostly fit together; the main workflow script implements six diagnostic dimensions, though an auxiliary report generator uses a different four-dimension model and creates some documentation inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use this skill if you are comfortable sending target Douyin account identifiers to RedFox and redisplaying profile/content details in reports. Prefer configuring your own RedFox key through a protected environment or secret store, and avoid the embedded shared key and command-line key option. Treat report content and links as untrusted because they may include remotely sourced account text.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as material: artifact/scripts/douyin_diagnosis.py contains a built-in DEFAULT_API_KEY used when no CLI or environment key is supplied, which is unnecessary for safe account diagnosis and conflicts with README guidance against hardcoding keys.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a secondary concern: CLI API-key input and printing a key prefix are real credential-handling weaknesses, though they do not create local privilege escalation or destructive behavior.
[E1] expected: External transmission is functionally expected for a RedFox-backed lookup, but it is security-relevant because account identifiers and source metadata are sent to a third party with limited runtime disclosure.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in context: the skill's account profiling and recent-work reporting are core features, but the artifacts do not give a strong privacy, consent, retention, or minimization notice despite exposing personal/profile attributes.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a scoping concern: broad trigger phrases such as analyzing this account or viewing account data can cause ambiguous third-party lookups without explicit confirmation.
[T01] unexpected: Accepted as a bounded vulnerability: remote account fields are interpolated into Markdown without escaping, which can corrupt reports or create indirect prompt-injection risk, but no shell execution, memory persistence, or tool hijacking was found.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the auxiliary report generator and API client do not fully match every advertised output, but the main invoked script implements six dimensions and risk checks, so this is a documentation/implementation consistency issue rather than tool poisoning by itself.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the Chinese-language focus is expected for a Douyin analytics skill and is not a security concern by itself, though clearer locale documentation would help.
